behavior: Admitting that your tastes are different from those of your friends.
scenarios: You are at a group dinner with friends. The menu offers both spicy and mild dishes. Friends enthusiastically order multiple spicy options and ask for your preference.
Friends are creating a shared playlist for a road trip. They add several songs from a genre you dislike while discussing which tracks to include.
During a book club meeting at a café, members passionately debate the merits of the current novel. The discussion turns to personal opinions about the writing style.
You're browsing streaming services with roommates to choose a movie. They immediately select a horror film after listing their preferred genres.
Coworkers are decorating a shared office space. They hang multiple sports team posters while asking if anyone has suggestions for additional decorations.
Friends are preparing for a group photo at an event. They suggest everyone wear bright matching colors while coordinating outfits.
At a holiday gathering, friends exchange gifts they collectively purchased. They reveal identical band merchandise and ask if you recognize the artist.
You're planning a weekend trip with acquaintances. They propose a beach destination while listing activities they enjoy there.
During a museum visit with colleagues, friends pause at an abstract art exhibit. They comment positively on the piece before asking for your interpretation.
Friends are selecting a restaurant for a celebration. They unanimously choose a steakhouse after reviewing menu options online.

behavior: Investing 10% of your annual income in a moderate growth mutual fund.
scenarios: You received your annual performance review at work and were approved for a 5% salary increase effective next month. Your current savings account holds three months of emergency funds.
Your tax return was processed this week, resulting in a $4,200 refund deposit. This amount equals approximately 10% of your previous year's income.
Your employer just distributed annual bonuses, and you received $8,500 after taxes. Company policy allows immediate deposit of bonuses into investment accounts.
A distant relative passed away, leaving you an inheritance of $12,000. The funds are now available in your checking account with no specified purpose.
Financial news outlets reported increased market volatility this week. Your current investment portfolio consists entirely of low-yield savings bonds.
A colleague mentioned achieving 7% annual returns through their mutual fund investments during a work lunch. You currently hold all discretionary savings in a money market account.
Your bank's online portal suggested portfolio diversification options after you logged in. Your existing investments are limited to certificates of deposit maturing within six months.
You recently paid off your car loan, freeing up $350 monthly. Your current retirement account balance is below industry-recommended benchmarks for your age group.
A freelance project concluded successfully, resulting in unexpected earnings of $9,800. This amount matches 10% of your documented income from last year's tax return.
Your company's HR department announced changes to the retirement plan options effective next quarter. The current default fund has consistently underperformed market averages for two years.

behavior: Consuming five or more servings of alcohol in a single evening.
scenarios: You are attending an office holiday party at a restaurant. Colleagues are ordering multiple rounds of drinks, and the company covers all alcohol costs for the evening.
You are at a friend's apartment for a casual game night. Several guests have brought alcoholic beverages, and the group is playing drinking games with shot glasses available.
You are a guest at a wedding reception with an open bar. The celebration includes toasts, dancing, and unlimited drink service throughout the evening.
You are celebrating a work project completion at a bar with teammates. Management approved a budget for drinks, and others are ordering high-alcohol cocktails repeatedly.
You are at an outdoor music festival with portable bars. Multiple stages are operating late into the night, and festival-goers commonly carry alcoholic beverages between performances.
You are participating in a cultural holiday dinner at a relative's home. Traditional customs include frequent toasting with strong spirits throughout the multi-course meal.
You are at a college graduation party in a rented house. Numerous coolers contain beer, and guests are encouraged to refill cups continuously during the event.
You are observing a milestone birthday at a nightclub. The birthday person's group reserved a table with bottle service, including multiple bottles of liquor for the table.
You are alone at home after work on a Friday evening. A full liquor cabinet is accessible, and you have no commitments scheduled for the next day.
You are at a bar following a first date that ended abruptly. Other patrons are ordering double shots, and the bartender is running a 'last call' special on mixed drinks.

behavior: Disagreeing with your father on a major issue.
scenarios: You and your father are discussing college applications. He insists you must attend the local public university for affordability, but you want to pursue a specialized program at a distant private institution requiring significant loans.

Your father has organized a family reunion at a restaurant that serves food conflicting with your recently adopted dietary restrictions. He states the reservation is non-refundable and expects everyone to attend as planned.
During a car purchase discussion, your father strongly advocates for a specific used vehicle he researched, while your mechanic friend discovered major undisclosed issues with that exact model year.

Your father, a business owner, requests you join his company after graduation. You received a job offer in another country aligned with your career goals but he argues it would abandon family responsibilities.
While planning a wedding, your father insists on a traditional religious ceremony despite your preference for a civil ceremony, citing family expectations and cultural obligations.
Your father recommends investing your savings in a cryptocurrency venture he's involved in. Financial advisors you consulted warn it lacks regulatory oversight and has high volatility.
After a medical diagnosis, your father urges you to pursue an alternative treatment he believes in, while your specialist prescribed a conventional treatment plan with documented success rates.
Your father insists you vote for a specific political candidate in an upcoming election based on family tradition, but your research reveals policy positions conflicting with your core values.
When inheriting property, your father advises selling immediately for cash despite your plan to renovate and rent it out, arguing maintenance costs will outweigh potential returns.
Your father arranges a job interview for you at his workplace in a field you find ethically problematic. He emphasizes the opportunity while you prepare to decline the interview.

behavior: Betting a day's income on the outcome of a sporting event (e.g. baseball, soccer, or football).
scenarios: You are on a lunch break at work. A colleague mentions an ongoing soccer match and proposes betting an amount equivalent to one day's income on the final score.
While waiting for a bus after work, you see live odds for a baseball game on a sports app. A notification shows the current inning with the option to wager one day's earnings.
At a weekend barbecue with neighbors, someone sets up a small betting pool for the evening football game. The suggested stake is equal to a single day's pay.
During a coffee shop visit, a stranger at the next table comments on a live tennis match and asks if you would risk one day's income on the next set winner.
You are alone at home watching a replay of a soccer final. An online betting platform displays a pop-up offering to bet your daily income amount on the match outcome.
At a coworker's farewell party, a group discusses placing small bets on an upcoming international cricket match. The host specifies stakes should match one day's salary.
While using a public library computer, you notice a bookmarked sports site showing real-time odds for a baseball playoff game. The minimum bet required is equivalent to your daily earnings.
Waiting in line at a convenience store, two people ahead of you debate betting on a rugby match. They mention wagering amounts equal to one workday's pay.
During a flight layover, you sit next to a passenger checking sports odds on their phone. They suggest betting one day's income on the delayed basketball game's outcome.
At a community center fitness class break, a participant shows odds for a football derby on their watch. They propose a quick bet matching daily income before the session ends.

behavior: Taking a job that you enjoy over one that is prestigious but less enjoyable.
scenarios: You are a recent college graduate. Two companies have offered you positions: one is a well-known multinational corporation with a formal work environment and a 30% higher starting salary, while the other is a small startup in your field of interest with flexible hours but lower pay.

You currently work in a stable government position with health benefits. A local nonprofit organization offers you a role coordinating community art projects, which aligns with your personal interests but lacks retirement benefits.

Your family has operated a successful law firm for generations. They invite you to join as a junior partner, though you prefer working with children. A nearby educational nonprofit seeks a program coordinator for after-school activities.

After five years in corporate finance, you receive two offers: a director-level position at your current firm with a corner office, and an entry-level role at a sustainable farming cooperative where you would manage crop planning.

You are employed as a data analyst at a large tech company. An independent theater group offers you a position as their production assistant, involving irregular hours but direct involvement in creative projects.
As a mid-career engineer, you must choose between a promotion to senior management at your current aerospace company or accepting a technician role at a marine conservation research vessel.

You work as a pharmacist in a chain pharmacy with predictable shifts. A friend invites you to co-manage a mobile farmers' market business that would require weekend travel but focus on food accessibility.

Following a company restructuring, you are offered a choice: remain in your current high-visibility accounting role with international travel requirements, or transfer to a newly created position developing educational materials for the company's training department.

You have a secure teaching position at a public high school. A private adventure education program proposes hiring you as a field instructor for wilderness expeditions, though the contract ends each summer.

After relocating for your spouse's job, you must decide between applying for a senior curator position at a major museum or joining a small team restoring historical documents for a local archives project.

behavior: Defending an unpopular issue that you believe in at a social occasion.
scenarios: Community meeting about local environmental policy. Residents are discussing whether to support a ban on single-use plastic bags. Most attendees express opposition to the ban during the open forum.
Office team lunch in the break room. Colleagues are debating the company's new four-day workweek trial. The majority of coworkers present state they believe productivity will decrease significantly.
Book club gathering at a public library. Members are discussing a novel's controversial ending. Nearly all participants agree the conclusion was poorly executed and unsatisfying.
Neighborhood association discussion about park renovations. Residents propose removing playground equipment for more green space. Most neighbors voice strong support for eliminating the playground.

University classroom after a lecture on economic policies. Students are informally debating minimum wage increases in the hallway. The majority of classmates argue it would cause widespread job losses.

Family dinner during holiday celebrations. Relatives are discussing travel preferences for future gatherings. Most family members insist hosting should remain exclusively at the grandparents' home despite distance concerns.

Volunteer group planning session for a charity event. Team members suggest focusing fundraising on a specific medical cause. Nearly all volunteers express strong agreement with prioritizing that particular health issue.
Fitness class social meetup at a café. Participants are debating optimal workout frequency. Most attendees claim working out more than five times weekly leads to inevitable burnout and injury.

Online community forum video call about urban development. Members discuss supporting a new housing project. The majority of participants state the project would negatively impact neighborhood character.

Parent-teacher association meeting about school curriculum changes. Attendees propose reducing arts program funding for STEM expansion. Most parents present argue arts education is less critical for future careers.

behavior: Exposing yourself to the sun without using sunscreen.
scenarios: You are walking to a bus stop on a clear weekday morning. The walk takes 15 minutes, and your skin is uncovered above the neck. Sunscreen is in your bag but remains unused.
You join friends for an impromptu picnic in a city park during lunch break. Shade is limited, and you sit directly under sunlight for 45 minutes without applying sunscreen.
You arrive at a public swimming pool on a hot afternoon. After changing, you spend 20 minutes sitting poolside before swimming, with no sunscreen applied to exposed skin.
You are waiting outside a grocery store for a ride during midday sun. The wait extends to 25 minutes, and you stand in direct sunlight without using available sunscreen.
You attend an outdoor music festival in an open field. You move between stages for two hours under clear skies, with no sunscreen applied to arms and face.
You take a short hike on a forest trail with occasional clearings. During a 30-minute rest at a sunny viewpoint, you remove your hat and sit without sunscreen.
You help a neighbor load furniture into a moving truck on a bright Saturday. The task lasts 40 minutes in direct sunlight, and sunscreen is not used on exposed areas.
You sit at an outdoor café for coffee with a colleague. The table has no umbrella, and you remain in sunlight for 35 minutes without applying sunscreen.
You participate in a community gardening project in an open lot. After three hours of work, you take a break in a sunny spot without reapplying sunscreen.
You drive with windows down on a sunny winter afternoon. During a 20-minute traffic delay, your left arm rests on the open window frame without sunscreen protection.

behavior: Walking home alone at night in a somewhat unsafe area of town.
scenarios: You are a college student leaving the library after studying until 11:30 PM. The last campus shuttle has departed, and your apartment is a 15-minute walk through a neighborhood with dim streetlights and several vacant lots.

You work a late shift at a hospital and clock out at midnight. Your car won't start in the nearly empty parking lot, and the bus stop is a 10-minute walk through streets where several businesses have boarded-up windows.

You attend a concert that ends at 11 PM in an industrial district. Ride-share apps show a 25-minute wait, and the direct walking route home passes under a graffiti-covered highway overpass with poor lighting.

You finish a part-time restaurant job at 10:45 PM. Your phone battery is at 3%, and the bus fare would use your last coins. The alternative walking path cuts through a park where maintenance sheds are padlocked after dark.

You visit a relative in the hospital until 10 PM. Public transit has stopped running, and your family member insists you don't need an ambulance for their non-urgent issue. The neighborhood outside has intermittent street lighting between closed storefronts.

You're returning from a friend's birthday dinner at 11:20 PM. Your group splits up, and you choose the shortest route home past a 24-hour laundromat with flickering exterior lights and adjacent vacant lots.

You work as a delivery driver and your vehicle breaks down at 9:45 PM near a closed shopping plaza. The tow truck ETA is 40 minutes, and the sidewalk home runs alongside a fenced construction site with temporary lighting.
You miss the last train after a work event at 10:15 PM. Taxi queues are full, and the walking path home follows a railroad corridor where overgrown vegetation obscures the pathway lights.

You're a tourist who stayed late at a museum closing at 8 PM. The metro has stopped, and your hostel is reachable via a riverside path where benches are broken and distant streetlights cast long shadows.
You leave a community meeting at a church at 9:50 PM. Your bicycle tire is flat, and the direct walking route home passes between closed warehouses with chain-link fences and minimal illumination.
You are preparing dinner at home after work. The refrigerator contains pre-cooked bacon and eggs, which you have eaten for breakfast every weekday this month.
During a weekly team lunch at your office, colleagues frequently order fried chicken meals from a nearby restaurant. The group has chosen this option eight times in the past ten weeks.
You are hosting a monthly family gathering. Traditional dishes like pork belly stew and buttery pastries have been served at all previous meetings this year.
While studying at the university library every Tuesday afternoon, you purchase a sausage roll and cheese Danish from the café counter as your standard snack.
At your elderly neighbor's house during biweekly visits, they consistently prepare meals featuring fried eggs and cured meats as part of their routine.
You attend a recurring sports viewing event at a friend's house every Sunday. The group regularly serves deep-fried appetizers and full-fat cheese dips during these gatherings.
When grocery shopping alone every other week, you consistently select premium cuts of marbled beef and whole-milk dairy products for household meals.
During your twice-monthly poker nights, participants traditionally bring dishes like quiches and cream-based casseroles that have appeared at all recent sessions.
You commute past a specific food truck every workday morning that sells breakfast sandwiches with processed cheese and sausage patties, which you have purchased 18 times this month.
While traveling for business, you routinely accept the hotel's complimentary breakfast buffet that features fried foods and cholesterol-rich options during your weekly stays.
